messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: service=continuous-batcher cluster=us-east-1 symptom=high-latency+OOM count=23

sam: saw this spike, paging oncall. latency to token completion jumped from ~50ms -> 2s and some pods OOMed.

li: attaching recent node logs and stack trace. looks like repeated `cudaMalloc` failures followed by container restart loop. also seeing queue depth metric steadily climb to >10k.

li: ```
2026-03-14T04:02:11Z continuous-batcher[pid=4212]: ERROR cuda: out of memory when allocating 512MB
2026-03-14T04:02:11Z continuous-batcher[pid=4212]: batcher: queue_len=11234 current_batch_size=2048
2026-03-14T04:02:12Z kubelet: container exited code=137
```

kevin: this matches the continuous-batcher-growth bug we've seen in staging. queue not honoring max_batch_size -> unbounded accumulation -> backend attempts huge allocations -> OOM.

anya: confirming customer impact. CS reported a handful of production requests timing out and one enterprise customer saw 500s on their embed job. @cs-rep any logs from them?

cs-rep: customer reported intermittent 503s starting ~03:58 UTC, spike lasted ~12m. they flagged retries triggered and some downstream queues backed up.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) throttle ingress to batcher 2) kill one offending node pod to break deadlock 3) enable fallback to smaller model (quantized) for affected route 4) start rolling restart of pool with patched env var to enforce batch_size cap. suggestions?

kevin: agree. quick commands:
```sh
# set temporary request limit on nginx route
curl -X POST "https://api.internal/routes/continuous-batch/limits" -d '{"rps": 50}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN"

# cordon a node to force scheduler to redistribute
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-12.us-east-1
kubectl delete pod continuous-batcher-xyz -n inference
```

```
# toggle fallback route to small-model v2
PATCH /v1/routes/continuous-batch
{
  "fallback_model": "small-model-v2",
  "fallback_enabled": true
}
```

anya: I'll flip the fallback now. doing config patch... done. traffic shifted to small-model-v2 for that route, watching error rate.

infra-bot: restart job queued: rollout/continuous-batcher pool=fast-gpu strategy=restart by anya at 2026-03-14T04:08:30Z

deploy-bot: pod continuous-batcher-xyz terminated by user request (deleted). new pod scheduling on node ip-10-0-6-21.

li: after restart, queue_len fell from 11k -> 120 within 90s. memory alloc errors stopped. however saw a secondary node flap: ip-10-0-6-21 reported GPU driver kernel oops then recovered.

kevin: GPU driver oops could be correlated to very large batch kernel selection — suggests we need a runtime guard to refuse batches above X tokens or to force CPU fallback for oversized batches. i'll draft quick patch.

sam: handoff: I'm going offline in 15m. kevin, can you own post-incident followup and mitigation rollout? include SLO impact calc and customer outreach notes. I'll do initial incident report and timeline.

kevin: taking it. immediate todo: 1) merge guard in runtime to cap batch at 2048 tokens 2) add circuit breaker: if cudaMalloc fails 3 times in 60s, force fallback model for that pool 3) add metric alert on queue_len > 2000.

nora: notifying affected customer with summary and mitigation steps. ETA on full revert/patch?

kevin: patch -> test -> canary in staging in 2 hours, production rollout after 30m of green metrics. if need be we can enforce soft cap via env var earlier.

anya: for the incident record: severity=P2 (partial customer impact), duration ~18m from first error to stabilized. impacted routes: /v1/continuous-batch (some enterprise customers), affected region: us-east-1.

sam: adding handoff note: observed symptoms -> queue growth -> cuda OOM -> pod crash loops -> node driver glitch -> restart broke the chain -> fallback reduced impact. Followups assigned to kevin.

kevin: creating GH issue now and adding repro notes. snippets I ran to reproduce locally attached in the issue (batcher config + stress script).

li: leaving logs and pprof snapshots in /mnt/logs/incidents/1823456789 for postmortem.

nora: CS updated customer at 04:35 UTC, offered 10% service credit and prioritized follow-up.

sam: ok handoff complete. if anything spikes ping @kevin directly. otherwise i'll pick up the postmortem template tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated by manual rollback and fallback. severity=P2 closed to monitoring.
